quote: expect 2007 to be the year in which many brands realize (if not grudgingly accept) that the ‘old’, mass-era status symbols, from the Audi Q7 to the De Beers Radiance collection, are no longer every consumers’ wet dream.
note: Trend label: STATUS LIFESTYLES. Sub-lifestyles listed: TRANSIENT, PARTICIPATIVE, CONNECTING (part of ONLINE), ECO-LIFESTYLES.

quote: 2007 could be the year in which TRANSPARENCY TYRANNY really starts scaring the shit out of non-performing brands.
note: Trend label: TRANSPARENCY TYRANNY. Sub-themes: multimedia and real-time reviews, PROFILE MANIA, paid contributors, niche price comparison, group buying (CROWD CLOUT).

quote: 2007 will see a broad debate on what constitutes web 3.0, web 4.0 and who knows, even web 5.0.
note: Trend label: WEB N+1.

quote: experienced consumers are trying out new appliances, new services, new flavors, new authors, new destinations, new artists, new relationships, new *anything* with post mass-market gusto.
note: Trend label: TRYSUMERS. Quote is part of the edition's 'beta-definition' of TRYSUMERS.

quote: This year, expect many corporations, small and big, to aggressively court the 1% of most creative and experienced individuals roaming the globe.
note: Trend label: THE GLOBAL BRAIN. 'This year' is 2007 (edition date January 2007).

quote: We've dubbed the above phenomenon STATUS SPHERES: a variety of lifestyles, activities and persuasions, which can be mixed and matched by consumers looking for recognition from various crowds and scenes.
note: Trend label: STATUS SPHERES. Spheres listed: traditional, transient, online, eco, giving, participative. Successor of 2007 STATUS LIFESTYLES (the text says so).

quote: no industry, no sector, no product will escape a premium version in the next 12 months.
note: Trend label: PREMIUMIZATION.

quote: SNACK CULTURE, like PREMIUMIZATION, is not a 'new new ' trend, but definitely one that will continue to thrive next year.
note: Trend label: SNACK CULTURE.

quote: Five years ago, we introduced ONLINE OXYGEN as the engine behind all this excitement: control-craving consumers needing online access as much as they need oxygen.
note: Trend label: ONLINE OXYGEN. Recycled label: ONLINE OXYGEN was a 2003 monthly briefing. The section cites third-party mobile forecasts (about 3.3 billion mobile users in 2011; nearly 1 in 3 mobile subscribers on mobile broadband by 2012), not trendwatching's own numbers.

quote: Eco-friendly goods and services sporting bold, iconic design and markers, that help their eco-conscious owners to visibly tout their eco-credentials to peers.
note: Trend label: ECO-ICONIC. Quote is the edition's own definition, printed in quotation marks.

quote: Instead of stalking potential and existing customers (which is not very 2008), why not assist them in smart, relevant ways, making the most of your products and whatever it is your brand stands for?
note: Trend label: BRAND BUTLERS.

quote: In fact, expect MIY | MAKE IT YOURSELF (and then SIY | SELL IT YOURSELF) ventures to become increasingly sophisticated in the next 12 months:
note: Trend label: MIY | MAKE IT YOURSELF. Quote ends with a colon in the source (it introduces examples).

quote: when co-creating, co-funding, co-buying, co-designing, co-managing *anything* with 'crowds', the emphasis in 2008 will move from just getting the masses in, to mining those crowds for the rough and polished diamonds.
note: Trend label: CROWD MINING.

quote: NICHETRIBUTES are attributes / features / additions to existing products, making them more practical for specific user groups, while at the same time signaling to those users that the brand 'gets it’, that it cares, and in some cases even pays tribute to their lifestyle.
note: Trend label: NICHETRIBUTES. Heading subtitle: 'Low-cost, practical tributes to the zeitgeist'.

quote: So in 2009, instead of worrying about missing out on the next big thing in luxury, focus on defining it.
note: Trend label: LUXYOURY. Heading subtitle: 'In 2009, you decide what constitutes luxury'.

quote: FEEDBACK 3.0 is one of the trends-within-a-trend that is starting to make waves.
note: Trend label: FEEDBACK 3.0. Heading subtitle: 'Think we've reached full transparency? You ain't seen nothing yet'. Sub-trend of TRANSPARENCY TYRANNY (2007).

quote: ECONCIERGES are firms and services dedicated to helping households go green in any possible way.
note: Trend label: ECONCIERGE. Heading subtitle: 'Forget spending, eco will be about saving or even making'.

quote: any consumer-focused brand would be stupid not to be partnering or experimenting with map-based services.
note: Trend label: MAPMANIA. Heading subtitle: 'Why the maps are the new interface'. Text cites Nokia expecting half of its handsets to be GPS enabled by 2010-2012 (Nokia's expectation, not trendwatching's).

quote: 2009 will be an excellent year for those businesses keen on showing consumers that they really care.
note: Trend label: HAPPY ENDING. Heading subtitle: 'The silver linings of each downturn'. Umbrella theme for the other five.

quote: For the first time, there’s a global understanding, if not a feeling of urgency that sustainability, in every possible meaning of the word, is the only way forward.
note: Trend label: BUSINESS AS UNUSUAL. Preceded by 'In 2010, prepare for 'business as unusual'.'

quote: A defining trend for 2010, 2011, 2012, and so on: urbanization on steroids.
note: Trend label: URBANY. Section quotes a third-party figure: urban share of world population exceeded 50 per cent in 2008 (past, not a forecast).

quote: let’s dive into one sub-trend that will be truly disruptive: the rise of REAL-TIME REVIEWS.
note: Trend label: REAL-TIME REVIEWS. Sub-trend of NOWISM.

quote: In 2010, luxury, and what it means to a bewildering number of ‘consumer segments’, will remain in flux.
note: Trend label: (F)LUXURY.

quote: More people than ever will be living large parts of their lives online in 2010. Yet, those same people will also mingle, meet up, and congregate more often with other ‘warm bodies’ in the offline world .
note: Trend label: MASS MINGLING. Source has a space before the final full stop.

quote: serious eco-results will depend on making products and processes more sustainable without consumers even noticing it
note: Trend label: ECO-EASY. Quote is the first clause of a longer sentence.

quote: If INFOLUST (consumers lusting after relevant information) is the enduring mega trend, then TRACKING and ALERTING are its du jour sub-trends.
note: Trend label: TRACKING & ALERTING.

quote: It incorporates all giving initiatives that make giving and donating painless, if not automatic
note: Trend label: EMBEDDED GENEROSITY. 'It' is EMBEDDED GENEROSITY; the text says GENERATION G 'will be even bigger in 2010'.

quote: we're putting our money on data and profile mining by its rightful owners , i.e. consumers.
note: Trend label: PROFILE MYNING. Source has a space before the comma.

quote: Let’s face it: 2010 will be rawer, more opinionated, more risqué, more in your face than ever before.
note: Trend label: MATURIALISM. Recycled label: MATURIALISM was a 2004 monthly briefing.

quote: In 2011, there will be no excuses left not to be kind as a brand.
note: Trend label: RANDOM ACTS OF KINDNESS.

quote: Are you ready for hundreds of millions of more daring, more experienced consumers? And that's just one side effect of rapid global urbanization
note: Trend label: URBANOMICS. Follows URBANY (2010).

quote: Flash sales, group buying, GPS-driven deals: in 2011 pricing will never be the same
note: Trend label: PRICING PANDEMONIUM.

quote: In 2011, expect an increasing number of 'Western' brands to launch new products or even new brands dedicated (if not paying proper respect) to consumers in emerging markets
note: Trend label: MADE FOR CHINA (IF NOT BRIC).

quote: In 2011, you can’t go wrong supplying your (online-loving) customers with any kind of symbol, virtual or 'real world', that helps them display to peers their online contributions, creations or popularity
note: Trend label: ONLINE STATUS SYMBOLS.

quote: growing numbers of consumers will expect health products and services in 2011 to prevent misery (if not improve their quality of life), rather than merely treating illnesses and ailments
note: Trend label: WELLTHY.

quote: SOCIAL-LITES are all about discovery, as consumers become curators; actively broadcasting, remixing, compiling, commenting, sharing and recommending content, products, purchases, experiences to both their friends and wider audiences
note: Trend label: SOCIAL-LITES AND TWINSUMERS. TWINSUMER was a 2005 monthly briefing.

quote: In 2011, brands and wealthy individuals from emerging markets (yes, especially China) will increasingly be expected to give, donate, care and sympathize versus just sell and take.
note: Trend label: EMERGING GENEROSITY.

quote: 2011 will see full-on PLANNED SPONTANEITY
note: Trend label: PLANNED SPONTANEITY. Recycled label: PLANNED SPONTANEITY was a 2002-2003 monthly briefing.

quote: When it comes to 'green consumption' in 2011, expect a rise in ECO-SUPERIOR products: products that are not only eco-friendly, but superior to polluting incumbents in every possible way
note: Trend label: ECO SUPERIOR. Heading prints 'ECO SUPERIOR'; the text prints 'ECO-SUPERIOR'.

quote: 2011 could be the year when sharing and renting really tips into mainstream consumer consciousness
note: Trend label: OWNER-LESS.

quote: In 2012, department stores, airlines, hotels, theme parks, museums, if not entire cities and nations around the world will roll out the red carpet for the new emperors, showering Chinese visitors and customers with tailored services and perks, and in general, lavish attention and respect.
note: Trend label: RED CARPET.

quote: Expect to see consumers take advantage of new technologies and apps to discreetly and continuously track, manage and be alerted to, any changes in their personal health.
note: Trend label: DIY HEALTH.

quote: In 2012, not only will consumers continue to hunt for deals and discounts, but they will do so with relish if not pride.
note: Trend label: DEALER-CHIC.

quote: Brands will increasingly take back all of their products for recycling (sometimes forced by new legislation), and recycle them responsibly and innovatively.
note: Trend label: ECO-CYCOLOGY.

quote: But a cashless future is (finally) upon us, as major players such as MasterCard and Google work to build a whole new eco-system of payments, rewards and offers around new mobile technologies.
note: Trend label: CASH-LESS. Preceded by 'Will coins and notes completely disappear in 2012? No.'

quote: the global opportunities for brands which cater to the hundreds of millions of lower-income CITYSUMERS are unprecedented.
note: Trend label: BOTTOM OF THE URBAN PYRAMID. Label printed two ways on the page: 'BOTTOM OF THE URBAN PYRAMID' (section heading, used here) and 'URBAN BOTTOM OF THE PYRAMID' (overview); abbreviated BOUP.

quote: Anything that makes it downright simple- if not completely effortless- for consumers to contribute to something will be more popular than ever in 2012.
note: Trend label: IDLE SOURCING.

quote: Why to consumers, brands that behave more humanly, including exposing their flaws, will be awesome.
note: Trend label: FLAWSOME. The sentence reads oddly in the source ('Why to consumers'); kept verbatim.

quote: Thanks to the continued explosion of touchscreen smartphones, tablets, and the 'cloud', 2012 will see a SCREEN CULTURE that is not only more pervasive, but more personal, more immersive and more interactive than ever.
note: Trend label: SCREEN CULTURE.

quote: In 2012, ‘trading in’ is the new buying.
note: Trend label: RECOMMERCE.

quote: Expect frank, risqué or non-corporate products, services and campaigns from emerging markets to be on the rise in 2012.
note: Trend label: EMERGING MATURIALISM. Extends MATURIALISM (2004, 2010).

quote: 2012 will see instant visual information gratification brought into the real and visual world with objects and even people.
note: Trend label: POINT & KNOW.

quote: expect pre-ordering, crowdfunding and consumer equity to compete with traditional consumption in 2013
note: Trend label: PRESUMERS & CUSTOWNERS.

quote: it's now time to get ready for an explosion in products and services from emerging markets for emerging markets
note: Trend label: EMERGING². Label prints a superscript 2 ('EMERGING squared').

quote: in 2013, consumers will look to their mobile devices to maximize absolutely every moment , multi-if-not-hypertasking their experiences, purchases and communications
note: Trend label: MOBILE MOMENTS.

quote: One sign-of-the-times eco-trend for 2013: the phenomenon of products and services that quite literally contain new life inside.
note: Trend label: NEW LIFE INSIDE.

quote: In 2013, expect consumers to turn to the medical profession and medical institutions to certify and curate health apps and technologies, or to “prescribe” them, much as they prescribe medicines as part of a course of treatment
note: Trend label: APPSCRIPTIONS.

quote: Emerging markets will proudly export and even flaunt their national and cultural heritage in the next 12 months.
note: Trend label: CELEBRATION NATION.

quote: In 2013 expect savvy shoppers to start reversing the flow, as consumers seek to own and make the most of their lifestyle data
note: Trend label: DATA MYNING. Follows PROFILE MYNING (2010).

quote: to trigger a resurgence in domestic manufacturing in established markets in 2013
note: Trend label: AGAIN MADE HERE. Quote is the end of one long sentence listing the drivers (NEWISM, instant gratification, eco-concerns, stories, 3D printing).

quote: Brands must move from ‘having nothing to hide’ , to pro-actively showing and proving they have nothing to hide
note: Trend label: FULL FRONTAL.

quote: 2013 will see switched-on brands (i.e. brands that are embarking on the much-needed journey towards a more sustainable and socially-responsible future) demanding that their customers also contribute
note: Trend label: DEMANDING BRANDS.

quote: Indeed, GUILT-FREE STATUS will be the ultimate indulgence in 2014.
note: Trend label: GUILT-FREE STATUS. Teaser: 'Why in 2014, guilt-free is the new status symbol.'

quote: In 2014, more people will pool their data, their profiles, their preferences, in groups (small and big) to shape new goods and services.
note: Trend label: CROWD SHAPED.

quote: In 2014, perceptions of China will take another significant turn, as consumers come to realize China is fast becoming the epicenter of truly innovative, superior green consumer innovations, too*.
note: Trend label: MADE GREENER BY/FOR CHINA. The asterisk is in the source (footnote on MADE BETTER IN CHINA).

quote: Consumers will increasingly see their smartphones as devices for total lifestyle assistance.
note: Trend label: MYCHIATRY. Teaser: 'Why in 2014, mind will be the new body.'

quote: Why in 2014, delivering brilliant service without excessive data collection will earn you consumer trust (and profits won’t be far behind ;)
note: Trend label: NO DATA.

quote: Anything exceptional that ‘connected objects’ can do for consumers, whether that’s monitoring or improving health, helping them save money, getting chores done, will be warmly welcomed next year and beyond.
note: Trend label: THE INTERNET OF CARING THINGS. The section cites Gartner (October 2013): IoT adds USD 1.9 trillion of economic value in 2020; up to 30 billion connected devices in 2020. Gartner's forecasts, not trendwatching's; not recorded as metric.

quote: 2014 will see the consumer arena become even more global, local, flatter, cosmopolitan and so on.
note: Trend label: GLOBAL BRAIN. Section mainly announces trendwatching's own free regional Trend Bulletins (Asia, Africa, South & Central America). Same label as 2007 THE GLOBAL BRAIN with a different meaning.

quote: Why 2015's status-hungry prosumers will LOVE services that allow professional-quality output – minus the learning or time barriers.
note: Trend label: INSTANT SKILLS. Follows STATUS SKILLS (2006, 2007).

quote: In 2015, expect perennially time-starved customers to demand accelerated physical service options, especially from brands they extend their loyalty towards.
note: Trend label: FAST-LANING.

quote: 2015 will (finally!) be the year when mobile payment platforms become commonplace.
note: Trend label: FAIR SPLITTING. Section cites Juniper Research: 450 million mobile payment users forecast by 2017 (from 245 million at end-2013). Third-party forecast, not trendwatching's own; not recorded as metric.

quote: In 2015, the Internet of Things and the Sharing Economy collide to allow a whole new world of asset sharing: spontaneous, useful, fun, profitable and more.
note: Trend label: INTERNET OF SHARING THINGS. Label printed two ways: 'INTERNET OF SHARING THINGS' (section heading and intro, used here) and 'INTERNET OF SHARED THINGS' (overview list). Follows THE INTERNET OF CARING THINGS (2014).

quote: 2015 will be the year for progressive brands to initiate, undertake or support meaningful civic transformation.
note: Trend label: BRANDED GOVERNMENT.

quote: people – of all ages and in many markets – are constructing their own identities more freely than ever.
note: Trend label: POST-DEMOGRAPHIC CONSUMERISM. Refers to the November 2014 Trend Briefing of the same name.

quote: In search of wellness, strength, new skills, knowledge and more, 2015's consumers will embrace device-fueled rewards that incentivize improving behaviours.
note: Trend label: CURRENCIES OF CHANGE.

quote: Get ready for a wave of imaginative discounts that relieve lifestyle pain points or offer a helping hand in difficult times.
note: Trend label: SYMPATHETIC PRICING. Refers to the June 2014 Trend Briefing of the same name.

quote: many consumers will have their first face-to-face encounters with robots in 2015. And they'll enjoy them.
note: Trend label: ROBOLOVE. Section cites Amazon (10,000 Kiva robots by end-2014) and BCG (20-40% fulfillment cost cut); third-party figures, not recorded as metric.

quote: In 2015, winning brands will start contentious, painful and necessary conversations.
note: Trend label: BRAND STANDS.

quote: In 2016, consumers will embrace a new twist on a traditional form of cachet: exclusivity.
note: Trend label: STATUS TESTS.

quote: smart brands will focus on answering a more meaningful equation: innovative channels + nuanced contexts = right place + right time.
note: Trend label: CONTEXTUAL OMNIPRESENCE. Dek: 'Forget omnichannel. Get ready for new channels and new contexts.' Parent mega-trend is printed 'Helpfull'.

quote: One suggestion for 2016: turn inwards, and start by ensuring your internal culture is something to flaunt, rather than hide.
note: Trend label: INSIDER TRADING. Label printed 'Insider trading' in the nav and INSIDER TRADING in the body.

quote: In 2016, rising numbers of consumers will demand that brands use increasingly powerful and accessible artificial intelligence technologies to put truly smart products and services into their pockets, homes, inboxes, and more.
note: Trend label: BENEFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.

quote: Playfully reposition your product or service in order to offer PERSPECTIVE SHIFTS that shock customers into a radically new appreciation of the value you're offering .
note: Trend label: PERSPECTIVE SHIFTS. Parent mega-trend PRICING PANDEMONIUM was itself a 2011 trend.

quote: In 2017, the Experience Economy will gain a new dimension: that of the VIRTUAL EXPERIENCE ECONOMY.
note: Trend label: VIRTUAL EXPERIENCE ECONOMY. Dek: '2017's newest status symbol: digital experiences.'

quote: purposeful brands will find renewed opportunities in helping people understand their changing relationship to home
note: Trend label: WORLDS APART. Two sub-groups named: NEW GLOBAL CITIZENS and NATION NURTURERS.

quote: That’s why 2017 will see opportunities for brands, products and services that enable INCOGNITO INDIVIDUALS to be free.
note: Trend label: INCOGNITO INDIVIDUALS. Dek: 'Anonymity makes a comeback.'

quote: Which is why, in 2017 smart brands will broaden their thinking around sustainability and turn their attention to CAPACITY CAPTURE.
note: Trend label: CAPACITY CAPTURE.

quote: Customer expectations around these intertwined basic needs will reach new heights in 2017.
note: Trend label: BIG BROTHER BRANDS. Preceded by 'Convenience. Seamlessness. Relevance.' Dek: 'But this time, they'll be welcomed!' Section cites Tractica: digital virtual assistant users from 390 million (2015) to 1.8 billion worldwide by 2021; third-party forecast, not recorded as metric.

quote: Because in 2018, shoppers with more important things to do – and that’s all of them – will embrace the outsourcing of certain retail experiences to algorithms and smart devices.
note: Trend label: A-COMMERCE. Also printed as AUTOMATED COMMERCE.

quote: Post-demographic consumers – of all ages! – are crafting new narratives of adulthood. In 2018, they’ll look to brands to help.
note: Trend label: ASSISTED DEVELOPMENT.

quote: Because this is the year that millions of consumers start to feel it is possible to have a meaningful conversation (💖 a relationship, even 💖) with virtual entities that entertain, educate, heal and even befriend.
note: Trend label: VIRTUAL COMPANIONS. Dek: 'Virtual entities make the leap from assistants to companions.' Section cites Gartner's prediction that by 2020 the average person will have more conversations with bots than with their spouse; Gartner's claim, not recorded as metric. Emoji kept as printed.

quote: In 2018 they’ll expect all kinds of products and services to forgive them when their past – the product they selected, the size they chose, the service they wanted – doesn't match their future.
note: Trend label: FORGIVING BY DESIGN. Dek: 'Post-purchase forgiveness is 2018's must-have feature.'

quote: What kind of transparency WRECKING BALL is heading your way in 2018?
note: Trend label: GLASS BOX WRECKING BALLS. Dek: 'A revolution in transparency is just getting started.' Framed as a question; the trend claim is that radical transparency will expose internal cultures.

quote: In 2019, frustrated consumers will welcome LEGISLATIVE BRANDS: corporate interests using their significant power to call for, promote, and even impose laws that drive constructive change and make the world a better place.
note: Trend label: LEGISLATIVE BRANDS. Dek: 'Progressive consumers will welcome the 'law of the brand'.'

quote: In 2019, LAB RATS will see human wellness and lifestyle as an engineering problem to be solved.
note: Trend label: LAB RATS. Dek: 'Why an extreme test and fix mindset is the future of wellness.'

quote: That’s why in 2019, the boldest and most inspiring organizations will embrace OPEN SOURCE SOLUTIONS: sharing and even giving away their innovative solutions to our toughest shared problems.
note: Trend label: OPEN SOURCE SOLUTIONS. Dek: 'A bold new frontier for sustainability.'

quote: In 2019, rising numbers of consumers will demand SUPERHUMAN RESOURCES: ethical AI and algorithms that deliver fair and unbiased decisions.
note: Trend label: SUPERHUMAN RESOURCES. Dek: 'It's time for our emerging AI overlords to play fair.'

quote: Yes, 24/7 connectivity and digital experiences that blur the boundaries of the real and virtual are not 'new' trends, but in 2019 their convergence will reach deeper than ever before into culture.
note: Trend label: FANTASY IRL. Dek: 'Imagined and real worlds collide in the name of play.'

quote: That’s why in 2020, millions of consumers will seek out products, services and experiences that help them alleviate rising eco-shame.
note: Trend label: GREEN PRESSURE. Dek: 'In 2020, consumers move from eco-status to eco-shame.'

quote: In 2020, consumers will pay deeper attention to brands who embody themselves via new virtual characters and avatars, allowing them to inhabit digital channels in richer, more immersive and more human ways.
note: Trend label: BRAND AVATARS. Dek: 'Human brands take powerful new form.'

quote: In 2020 consumers primed by constantly evolving digital services and smart physical spaces – and accustomed to the ultra-convenience of ‘everything as a service’ – will increasingly expect relevance as a service , too.
note: Trend label: METAMORPHIC DESIGN. Dek: 'Consumers demand relevance as a service.'

quote: In 2020, those consumers will look to brands to help them battle THE BURNOUT.
note: Trend label: THE BURNOUT. Dek: 'Smart brands rush to help those burned by the pressures of modern life.' Section cites survey data (Microsoft, Cigna, National Working Families Report) about the present, not forecasts.

quote: In 2020 consumers will seek an antidote to vast and toxic online communities and social media platforms.
note: Trend label: CIVIL MEDIA. Dek: 'Why the future of social is meaningful connections.'

quote: We’re steadily moving towards people-first, car-free urban environments that prioritize wellbeing.
note: Trend label: 15-MINUTE CITIES. Subtitle: 'Boost urban wellbeing and community'.

quote: 2021 is about laying the groundwork for a more purposed recovery.
note: Trend label: PANDEMOMENT. Subtitle: 'Turn crisis into transformational opportunity'.

quote: In 2021, increasingly mindful people will look for products and services that seamlessly boost their mental wellbeing.
note: Trend label: DESIGNED FOR WELLBEING. Subtitle: 'Infuse mental wellness into your products'.

quote: The accelerated race to champion virtual events has only begun
note: Trend label: VIRTUALLY GROUNDED. Subtitle: 'Reimagine gatherings for today's mixed reality'.

quote: As longevity increases, people can, want and need to be productive for longer.
note: Trend label: OLD SPICE. Subtitle: 'Expand expertise by hiring older talent'.

quote: The plant-based revolution is hitting industries everywhere.
note: Trend label: PLANT-ED. Subtitle: 'Join the plant-based revolution'.

quote: In 2021, cynical consumers demand authentic social justice initiatives of, for and by those who have been sidelined.
note: Trend label: SYSTEMIC JUSTICE. Subtitle: 'Support and empower marginalized communities'.

quote: And in 2021, brands will increasingly make use of their waste to enter new markets.
note: Trend label: TRANSCYCLING. Subtitle: 'Use waste to enter new markets'.

quote: While fully autonomous cars are unlikely to roam the roads in 2021, we will see wider adoption of robots across different industries: in forests , on farms and in cities .
note: Trend label: ROBO-ROAMING. Subtitle: 'Adopt robots to automate and data-ify'.

quote: But offering support and assistance to former employees can be a big boost to the morale of current and future employees.
note: Trend label: TALENT TRANSFER. Subtitle: 'Care for employees, even after departure'.

quote: consider unconventional routes to building truly sustainable and ethical business operations.
note: Trend label: EXTRA-MILE SUSTAINABILITY. Subtitle: 'Take unconventional routes to greener products'.

quote: new norms — in gender, media, education and more — will dictate how brands communicate with their audiences, and what those audiences expect from brands.
note: Trend label: NORM RECALIBRATION. Subtitle: 'Accept, embrace and run with new norms'.

quote: Not just food brands, but restaurants and fashion brands are increasingly adopting carbon labelling to educate consumers on the hidden costs of products while gaining a new competitive advantage.
note: Trend label: CARBON LABELLING. Subtitle: 'Reveal true costs and gain consumer trust'.

quote: In 2021, the demand for creative ways to provide access to all will be higher than ever.
note: Trend label: DIGITAL PARITY. Subtitle: 'Providing online access to all'.

quote: Increasingly mindful shoppers demand that brands acknowledge the detrimental impact of hyperconsumerism and offer them more than just ‘more’.
note: Trend label: MINDSUMERS. Subtitle: 'Help consumers stop and (not) shop'.

quote: Enabling consumers to use virtual currency, goods and actions to achieve real-world impact is a surefire way to attract attention.
note: Trend label: BLURRED GAMING. Subtitle: 'Bring virtual playgrounds into 'real life''.

quote: Uncovering and transforming business models that are harmful to employees will be a leitmotif of the 2020s.
note: Trend label: WORKERS, INC.. Subtitle: 'Transform employees into owners'. Horizon in text: 'the 2020s'.

quote: In 2021, regenerative farming products will make their way into consumers' hands, giving early adopter brands a clear competitive advantage among eco-progressive consumers.
note: Trend label: EARTH POSITIVE. Subtitle: 'From climate neutral to regenerative'.

quote: As kids spend more time indoors looking at screens, analog home products that intrinsically spark learning and creativity are increasingly important.
note: Trend label: AMBIENT LEARNING. Subtitle: 'Spark learning through interior design'.

quote: In 2021, once-ridiculed lab-grown meat will make its way onto consumers' plates while accelerating the overhaul of the traditional livestock industry.
note: Trend label: LAB TO TABLE. Subtitle: 'Lab-grown meat is coming of age'.

quote: And creative solutions might end up improving your products and services for everyone.
note: Trend label: OMNI-ACCESSIBILITY. Subtitle: 'Design for people of all abilities'. The section states that 15% of the world's population has some form of disability (present figure, not a forecast).

quote: Recent lockdowns strengthened calls to improve the environmental and social fabric of cities.
note: Trend label: LOCALE MORALE. Opportunity #1 of 22. Subtitle: 'Made-to-measure communal improvements'.

quote: But as conscious consumerism gains ground, neighborhood shops stand a fighting chance.
note: Trend label: GLOCALLY GROUNDED. Opportunity #2 of 22. Subtitle: 'Boost offline shopping and local connections'. Second heading on the page prints 'GLOBAL GROUNDED LOCALLY'. Section cites a March 2021 survey (53% more interested in shopping locally); present figure.

quote: Consumers expect brands to wade in on front-page issues, but to create measurable impact, it’s crucial to support transformation at a grassroots level.
note: Trend label: EQUITY ZONE. Opportunity #3 of 22. Subtitle: 'Become a community catalyst'.

quote: The growing dissatisfaction with capitalist corruption is strengthening desire for local autonomy, with crowdsourced communities functioning as a resilient tool to achieve self-determination.
note: Trend label: COMMUNAL CURRENCIES. Opportunity #4 of 22. Subtitle: 'Keeping it in the community'.

quote: Pandemic lockdowns only strengthened calls to improve these localities and make them more livable, community-focused and resilient.
note: Trend label: STATE OF PLACE. Subtitle: 'Consumers look to reclaim their locale'. Mega-trend block summarising opportunities 1-4; the full mega-trend ('20+ sub-trends') is Premium only.

quote: It’s now about encouraging consumers to build a long-term, sustainable relationship with the products they buy from you.
note: Trend label: SECOND SOULS. Opportunity #5 of 22. Subtitle: 'Reuse and reimagine over repeat purchase'.

quote: As climate change continues to disrupt supply (even in highly developed countries), the number of power outages around the globe is expected to increase.

quote: Faced with apocalyptic headlines, consumers expect sustainability to be embedded in every product or service.
